title: Excessive parent account data stored in MongoDB
description: The Authentication Service stores parent account information to MongoDB users collection. This represents a data disclosure to the datastore. Threat exists if more personal data than necessary is stored, violating the minimality principle. Parent account data may include unnecessary fields that could be reduced.
assumptions: Parent account data contains personal information beyond what is strictly required for authentication purposes

title: Parent account data enables cross-account linking
description: Parent account information stored in MongoDB could enable linking of multiple user accounts or profiles together. This creates linkability risks where individual activities across different accounts could be correlated through the parent account relationship.
assumptions: Parent account data contains identifiers or relationships that connect multiple accounts

title: Parent account data enables individual identification
description: The parent account data stored in MongoDB users collection likely contains or enables identification of individuals. If this data is accessed or leaked, it could be used to identify specific users or account holders.
assumptions: Parent account data contains personally identifiable information or can be combined with other data to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized disclosure of JWT and user data during transmission

title: Identifiability of parent user through authentication data

title: Linkability of authentication sessions to parent user identity
